name: Japchae (Korean Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
why: Japchae is the ultimate Korean home-cook dish — sweet potato vermicelli tossed with shiitake, carrot and spinach in a soy-sesame glaze. It's a perfect fit for your current Korean phase, and everything's at its best right now with autumn spinach and shiitakes in season.
author: Henry
ingredients: 150g dried Korean sweet potato vermicelli noodles (dangmyeon)
1 carrot, peeled and cut into fine matchsticks
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked in warm water and sliced
1 tbsp vegetarian stir-fry sauce (vegetarian oyster sauce)

steps: Pour boiling water over the vermicelli in a large bowl and leave to soak for 6-8 minutes, until softened and still chewy. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Slice the onion, garlic and red pepper fine; cut the carrot into matchsticks; slice the soaked shiitake mushrooms; rough up the spinach leaves.
Mix the vegetarian stir-fry sauce, light soy sauce, sugar, vegetable stock and sesame oil together in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat until just smoking.
Stir-fry the onion for 30 seconds, then add the garlic, red pepper, carrot, mushrooms and spinach — allowing 30 seconds between each addition so the harder vegetables stay crisp.
Tip in the drained noodles and stir-fry for a further minute, folding everything through evenly.
Pour in the sauce and bring to a vigorous boil over high heat, stirring for 2-3 minutes until all the sauce has been absorbed by the noodles.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve straight from the wok, with a side of rice or kimchi if you like.

pro_tips: The 30-seconds-between-vegetables trick is the whole game — carrots and shiitake need the time, spinach just needs to wilt. Rush the order and you'll get soggy noodles with raw carrot.
If the drained vermicelli looks like it'll clump, give it a quick toss with a half teaspoon of sesame oil before it hits the wok — it separates beautifully and keeps that chewy bite.
